problemSignature.risk: A clean PCB/manufacturing ZIP can hide that the schematic is only a title-block shell.

rootCause: The fixture runner generated a valid routed PCB and manufacturing package but wrote a schematic shell instead of a real KiCad symbol/net graph. That made the board look product-complete while weakening schematic-to-PCB proof.
fixSummary: Generate embedded BoardForge fixture symbols, project-local KiCad symbol/footprint libraries, symbol instances, footprint properties, wires, global labels, and no-connect markers from the same component/net source used by PCB generation. Expose schematic graph counts in the manifest and routeability report.

testsAdded: fixture runner creates odd-shape preroute KiCad artifacts without fake manufacturing

conditions: BoardForge generates a new project from prompt
manufacturing readiness requires schematic plus PCB evidence
dashboard/status reports need to distinguish shell schematics from real graphs

recipe: Use a shared component/net model for schematic, PCB, BOM, and reports.
Generate KiCad embedded symbols with footprint properties.
Write project-local sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table, .kicad_sym, and .pretty footprint files.
Connect every routed net through global labels and wires.
Mark unused fixture pins with no-connect markers.
Add manifest evidence counters for symbols, global labels, wires, and no-connects.
Fail fixture tests if a manufacturing candidate regresses to a schematic shell.
safetyRules: Do not modify protected ESC or FC projects.
Do not export manufacturing unless KiCad validation and schematic evidence are honest.
